LESSON: CORRUPTION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: Muamalaat (Social Relations)
Topic 6.3: Corruption
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Corruption, part of Muamalaat (Social Relations) in Grade 6 ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: Why is corruption prohibited in Islam? 2) What can you do to stop corruption? 3) What are the effects of corruption in our society?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss forms of corruption in their environment (such as, exam cheating, inflating bus fare, withholding shopping balance, election, deceiving parents on school levies) and make brief presentation,

2. search for Hadiths/Qur’anic verses on corruption and write the teachings (Q. 2:11-12, 27, 30, 188),

3. brainstorm on the effects of corruption and display on charts,

4. design posters on ways of curbing corruption, 1)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss forms of corruption in their environment (such as, exam cheating, inflating bus fare, withholding shopping balance, election, deceiving parents on school levies) and make brief presentation,
2. search for Hadiths/Qur’anic verses on corruption and write the teachings (Q. 2:11-12, 27, 30, 188),
3. brainstorm on the effects of corruption and display on charts,
4. design posters on ways of curbing corruption, 1)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Corruption together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: listening, speaking, writing and teamwork skills attained through group discussions

and presentation.

• Critical thinking and problem solving: researching skill developed as learners search for Hadiths /Qur’anic verses on

corruption and write the teachings

• Citizenship as learners discuss upholding integrity

• Creativity and Imagination: there is networking as learners role-play the forms of corruption and design posters.

Values:
Integrity: Transparency and accountability as learners discuss the effects of corruption and ways of curbing it.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: Good governance enhanced as learners search for Hadiths /Qur’anic verses on corruption and write the teachings.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:


Remember the key question: Why is corruption prohibited in Islam? 2) What can you do to stop corruption? 3) What are the effects of corruption in our society?
